summary: Intermittent dedicated pool throughput sag correlated with suppressed tenant heartbeats ('heartbeat murmur')
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC InkScribe reported repeated p95/p99 throughput and latency degradation on their dedicated pool in us-west-2. The degradation appears intermittent (10-30 minute windows) and correlates with a subtle suppression of tenant heartbeat metrics across the pool — we are calling this pattern a 'heartbeat murmur'.

Impact: Customer experiences elevated request queuing and tail latency for batched routes (p99 generation time up to 6x baseline). Business impact: user-facing timeouts in their production inference pipelines; increased token cost due to queueing.

Background: InkScribe runs a mix of long-lived streams and many short-burst batched embedding calls. They are on a dedicated pool (reservation ID RP-4382) with pinned model redwood-v1-medium. No config changes on their side reported.

Observed behavior:
- Periodic windows (10–30m) where allocator shows fewer free GPU slots despite overall low global utilization.
- Tenant heartbeat rate dips (heartbeat/s) across several nodes simultaneously by ~30-60% for short intervals.
- Autoscaler responds by stretching warmup/scale decisions; some slots move to cooldown and reattach failures increase.

Expected behavior: Stable heartbeat stream from tenant side; allocator slot availability should reflect actual active connections. Autoscaler should not misclassify available capacity.

Notes: This is not a classic noisy-tenant CPU/GPU hog — metrics show low sustained kernel utilization on affected GPUs. The distinguishing signal is the heartbeat suppression and small but consistent KV-prefetch backlog growth during the murmur windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route InkScribe production traffic to dedicated pool RP-4382 in us-west-2 (mirror traffic if testing).
2) Run a mixed workload generator: 65% short embeddings (100ms payload) at 300 qps, 35% long-stream generation (keepalive) ~30 concurrent sessions per replica.
3) Observe allocator heartbeats, autoscaler decisions, and per-GPU slot counts over 30-90 minutes.
4) Compare p50/p95/p99 generation latency and queue length before, during, and after heartbeat dip windows.
logs: Sample allocator log snippet (2026-03-10T09:23:12Z): "attach_request timeout=120ms tenant=inkscribe session=abcd... reason=heartbeat-rate-low"
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Sophie Lin (Support): Acknowledged customer report and created ticket. Requesting telemetry from SRE for that time window.
2026-03-10 11:20 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Collected allocator + sidecar traces for 09:15-09:45 UTC. See attached logs. Initial observation: heartbeat meter drops precede attach timeouts by ~30s.
2026-03-10 12:03 - InkScribe (Customer): We've not changed SDKs or connection patterns. We'll provide client-side keepalive settings (current: keepalive=60s, heartbeat=15s).

2026-03-11 08:47 - Priya Shah (Platform): Hypothesis: telemetry emitter sidecar in the pool occasionally backs off during short IO stalls; this reduces perceived heartbeat and triggers autoscaler/allocator conservative behavior. Reproduced minor emitter stalls on dev nodes with a synthetic IO flood.

2026-03-12 09:30 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Pushed a telemetry sidecar patch (github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/4521) to staging to increase emitter queue capacity and added backoff smoothing. Monitoring staged pool for 24h before prod rollout.
investigation_notes: - Correlation matrix shows tenant_heartbeat_rate dip -> kv_prefetch_backlog increase -> allocator_free_slots drop -> autoscaler cooldown event (~+45s cascade).
- Sidecar logs show repeated transient EAGAIN when writing metrics aggregator socket during murmur windows (io_wait spikes on NVMe).
- GPUs show low compute duty cycle during windows, indicating slots are occupied/waiting rather than compute-bound. Kernel traces show idle wait for prefetch completion.
- Customer client keepalive is at 60s; heartbeat at 15s. When we simulated shorter client heartbeats (5s) the allocator recovered faster, suggesting sensitivity to heartbeat sampling.
resolution: Workaround (customer): Advise InkScribe to temporarily reduce client-side heartbeat interval to 5–10s and enable short-lived connection jitter to avoid synchronized quiet windows. This reduces attach timeout impact until platform fix rolls out.

Platform mitigation: Staged telemetry sidecar patch to increase emitter buffer and smooth backoff. Patch PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/4521. Will monitor staging pool RP-4382 for 24h; if stable, schedule canary to us-west-2 dedicated hosts during low-traffic window.

Permanent follow-ups: Product ticket to add allocator resilience for brief heartbeat suppression (add a 'soft-heartbeat' grace window), update autoscaler policy to consider KV-prefetch backlog signal, and run NVMe IO health check automation during maintenance windows. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: doc + plan by 2026-03-20.
Customer notified of workaround on 2026-03-10 13:00 UTC and will apply heartbeat change; they agreed to hold off high-volume rollout until confirmation of platform patch.
